title: Corran Valley Medical Centre: a 26-week slip and a claim due on 1 December
setting: Callerby Construct is a regional general contractor. It built Corran Valley Medical Centre, a four-storey steel-frame medical building, for the developer Halden Medical Properties under a £14.6m contract. The contract completion date was 30 April 2026. Practical completion came on 29 October 2026. Halden is deducting liquidated damages. Callerby's project director and a claims consultant have drafted a claim that blames the delay on Halden. Halden blames Callerby. The project's lender appointed an independent monitoring surveyor, and the project ran its information requests (RFIs) through a shared platform hosted by a third party. Callerby's Northern region also delivered Kestrel, a distribution warehouse, over the same period.
presentingRequest: Callerby's chief executive wants to know what actually caused the Corran Valley slip, and what Callerby should do about the drafted extension-of-time and prolongation claim, which is due to go to Halden on 1 December. She also wants to know what should happen inside the company.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Ruth Abernethy, chief executive, Callerby Construct, 12 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'Corran Valley Medical Centre reached practical completion on 29 October, 26 weeks after the contract date of 30 April. Halden is withholding £1.17m in liquidated damages. Our extension-of-time and prolongation claim for £1.9m is due to go to Halden on 1 December. Gareth says the slip is down to Halden's design changes and their architect's slow answers; Halden says the opposite. Before I sign anything I need to know what actually drove the slip and what we do next. On a brighter note, the Northern region had a good year: Kestrel warehouse handed over seven weeks early in March, and the regional early-handover incentive paid out to Colm Faraday's team.'

initialEvidence.source: Interview notes, Gareth Imrie, project director, 4 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: Says Halden 'redesigned the building while we were building it'. Cites six change orders, CO-07 to CO-12, including CO-09, which moved the MRI suite to level 2. Halden flagged it in September and it needed extra steel. 'We couldn't carry on with the frame until CO-09 was resolved, and the architect sat on our steel connection queries for weeks.' Confirms the tower crane went to the Kestrel job in October: 'Kestrel's hired crane failed its thorough examination, the region needed one, and ours was standing idle anyway. Colm and I agreed it.' Says he has 'had a word' with the site superintendent about 'chatting to Halden's clerk of works'.

initialEvidence.source: Draft claim summary, Fenmore Claims Advisory, prepared for Callerby, 28 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: The time impact analysis attributes the full 26-week delay to employer risk events: (a) owner change orders CO-07 to CO-12, issued 12 Sep–9 Dec 2025 and holding the structural frame: 17 weeks; (b) late information: 41 of 64 RFIs, including structural connection queries, open longer than the contractual response period: a further 9 weeks. RFI durations come from the 'created' date in the project RFI log. Programme inputs are the contractor's monthly updates. Claimed: a 26-week extension of time and £1.9m in prolongation costs. Engagement terms: Fenmore's fee includes 6% of sums recovered.

initialEvidence.source: Letter, Priya Varma, development manager, Halden Medical Properties, to Callerby, 10 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'We understand a delay claim is being prepared, so please note our position now. Your tower crane left site in October 2025 and did not come back until April. Your own superintendent told our clerk of works it had gone to another of your jobs. Our architect answered your queries promptly. The change orders concerned interior layouts and were small.' Halden will deduct liquidated damages in full and reserves its right to recover its own extra consultant and finance costs from Callerby.

initialEvidence.source: Interview notes, Dale Pruitt, site superintendent, 5 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'Autumn and winter were dead. The crane and the frame gang went over to Kestrel and we did bits: drainage, level 1 blockwork.' Asked why: 'Above my pay grade. Gareth and Colm sorted it.' Asked whether levels 3–4 could have gone up: 'Steel was on the ground. Whether every connection query was answered, I couldn't swear to; that's Gareth's side.' Recalls that steel deliveries for levels 1–2 were 'all over the place in the summer'. Confirms he told Halden's clerk of works where the crane had gone: 'He asked. I wasn't going to lie.'

initialEvidence.source: Callerby monthly progress report no. 14 to Halden, November 2025, signed G. Imrie
initialEvidence.text: 'Frame: level 3–4 erection resequenced pending resolution of CO-09 structural information and outstanding connection queries. Tower crane temporarily demobilised to reduce standing costs during the design hold.' The programme update moves frame completion from 19 Dec 2025 to 'TBC – subject to CO-09'. Stated critical path: CO-09 design → frame → envelope → fit-out. The report does not yet claim any change to the contract completion date.

catalogue.title: Halden Medical Properties board minutes, July–December 2025
catalogue.text: Extracts supplied by Halden. 22 Jul 2025: the board approves in principle moving the MRI suite from the ground floor to level 2; the architect is to advise on structure and cost. 16 Sep: approves a CO-09 budget of £212,000; the development manager is to notify the contractor. 18 Nov: notes the contractor's monthly report, which attributes the frame hold to CO-09; the development manager is 'to monitor and reserve position'. 9 Dec: approves CO-12, level 4 joinery, £38,000. No other programme discussion is recorded.

catalogue.title: Callerby plant ledger, tower crane TC-3, July 2025–June 2026
catalogue.text: Internal hire charges for company tower crane TC-3. Corran Valley cost code: 1 Jul–19 Oct 2025 and 31 Mar–26 Jun 2026. Kestrel warehouse cost code: 23 Oct 2025–20 Mar 2026. Dismantling, transport and re-erection charges (£46,800) were posted to Corran Valley. The 'approved by' field reads 'regional office' for both transfers. No transfer request forms are attached to the ledger.

catalogue.title: Public weather station summary, October 2025–April 2026
catalogue.source: Nearest public weather station, 6 km from site
catalogue.text: Rainfall for the period was 94% of the 30-year average. Five days had gusts above 38 mph, a typical tower crane wind limit. Three days had frost below –3°C. No named storms affected the area. The contract weather allowance for the period was 12 days.

catalogue.title: Lender's monitoring surveyor reports, October 2025–April 2026
catalogue.source: Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank
catalogue.text: Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank (Halden's lender); monthly reports, copied to both parties. 15 Oct 2025: frame on programme; level 3–4 steel delivered 6–14 Oct, stored on site; erection programmed from 21 Oct. 18 Nov: tower crane dismantled 20–22 Oct, 'required on another company project' per contractor; no erection since. CO-09 issued 6 Nov: four infill beams, level 2 only. 16 Dec: CO-09 beams installed 8–12 Dec using hired mobile crane; levels 3–4 untouched. Jan–Mar: no tower crane, no erection. 14 Apr 2026: crane re-erected 1–3 Apr; level 3 erection resumed 6 Apr. Completion forecast now 29 Oct 2026: frame delay plus cladding contractor's next slot (May). COs 07, 08, 10–12 are fit-out, not started, within float. Contractor's monthly factual-accuracy response: 'no comments'.

catalogue.title: Corran Valley site daily diaries, 20 October 2025–10 April 2026
catalogue.text: Typed by the assistant project manager and countersigned by the project director. 21 Oct: 'TC-3 dismantle. Frame on hold – design (CO-09).' Every entry from 22 Oct to 3 Apr repeats 'Frame: on hold – design', with daily labour of 9–14 (groundworks, drainage, level 1 blockwork). 10 Dec: 'Mobile crane – misc lifts.' 6 Apr: 'L3 steel erection commenced.' No entry says which design information was outstanding or when any of it arrived.

catalogue.title: Architect's change order register, CO-01 to CO-14
catalogue.text: The register lists 14 change orders with issue date, title and value. CO-07 (12 Sep 2025): level 4 partition layout, £61k. CO-08 (30 Sep): level 2 waiting area, £24k. CO-09 (6 Nov): MRI relocation, structural and M&E, £212k. CO-10 (14 Nov): level 2 nurse base, £17k. CO-11 (28 Nov): data cabling, £44k. CO-12 (9 Dec): level 4 joinery, £38k. The register contains no programme or time assessment.

catalogue.title: Callerby HR records, Corran Valley site management team, 2025–2026
catalogue.text: Site management team: project director, project manager, two site engineers, superintendent and assistant project manager. The project manager resigned in January 2026 and a replacement started in February 2026. Overtime, sickness absence and training hours were within company norms. One grievance was logged, about site parking, and resolved. No disciplinary records for the period.

catalogue.title: Tarrant Façades correspondence with Callerby, December 2025–May 2026
catalogue.text: 4 Dec 2025: 'We cannot start in January as programmed; the frame is incomplete. Please confirm a revised date.' 19 Feb 2026: 'Still no frame completion date. Our crews will be committed elsewhere until May.' 2 May 2026: confirms mobilisation and asks for £28,000 for remobilisation and the lost slot. The letters do not say why the frame was incomplete.

catalogue.title: Shared RFI platform export with audit timestamps, all project RFIs
catalogue.source: Project RFI platform, hosted by an independent software provider
catalogue.text: Users cannot edit the platform's audit trail. All 64 RFIs are included, each with 'created' (contractor draft opened), 'submitted' and 'answered' timestamps. Measured from submission, the architect's median response was 4 working days, and 62 of 64 were answered within the 10-working-day contract period. The two exceptions are RFI-052 (12 days) and RFI-058 (11 days), both on level 2 ceiling finishes in May 2026; the contractor marked both 'no programme impact' when submitting. Of the 41 RFIs the draft claim lists as late, 39 sat in contractor draft status for 9–47 days before submission. Structural RFIs, Oct 2025–Apr 2026: RFI-029 (submitted 2 Oct, answered 7 Oct), RFI-031 on CO-09 connections (10 Nov, 14 Nov), RFI-036 (28 Jan, 30 Jan).

catalogue.title: Corran Valley health and safety incident register, January 2025–October 2026
catalogue.text: Fourteen entries: nine first-aid cases; three near-misses, including a slewing incident during the 10 Dec 2025 mobile crane lift; and two reportable injuries during fit-out in August 2026 (a slip and a hand laceration). Each entry was closed with investigation notes. No regulator enforcement action is recorded.

catalogue.title: Fenmore Claims Advisory time impact analysis workbook
catalogue.text: The workbook behind the draft claim. Baseline: programme revision 3 (March 2025). Progress inputs: Callerby monthly programme updates nos. 12–24, as supplied by the project director. Delay fragments were inserted for CO-07 to CO-12 using the dates in the monthly reports, and for 'information delay' using RFI 'created' to 'answered' durations. Plant and crane availability are not modelled. Analyst note: 'Third-party contemporaneous records not reviewed; not supplied by client.'

catalogue.title: Callerby internal close-out report, Kestrel distribution warehouse, March 2026
catalogue.text: Handover on 13 Mar 2026, seven weeks ahead of contract. The client paid no early-completion bonus. The regional early-handover incentive was triggered for the Northern region team. Lifting: the hired crane was withdrawn after failing its thorough examination on 9 Oct 2025; company crane TC-3 was brought in from Corran Valley and erected 23–25 Oct. Lessons learned: 'secure backup crane options at tender stage.'

catalogue.title: Callerby anonymous staff survey 2026, Northern region results
catalogue.text: Response rate 58% (n=112). 'Resources are allocated fairly between projects': 31% agree (company 52%). 'I can raise programme concerns without fear': 44% agree (company 61%). Common free-text themes include 'targets' and 'pressure to hand over'. No breakdown by project is available.

catalogue.title: Local authority building control inspection records, Corran Valley
catalogue.text: Inspections were recorded for foundations (March 2025), drainage (April 2025) and fire stopping (August–September 2026). A completion certificate was issued on 27 Oct 2026. No frame-stage inspections are recorded, because the structural frame was certified by the contractor's engineer.

catalogue.title: Callerby group internal audit report on plant utilisation, February 2025
catalogue.text: Average tower crane utilisation across the group was 71%. Regional directors allocate cranes between projects with no group-level check on programme impact. The audit recommended central plant scheduling. Management response: 'Agreed, target Q4 2025.' Status in October 2026: not implemented.

hypotheses.text: Owner-directed design changes held up critical-path work.
Late responses from the owner's architect to the contractor's information requests held up critical-path work.
The contractor's redeployment of its own equipment or crews to other work held up critical-path work.
Late delivery of structural steel by the fabricator held up critical-path work.

edges.from: Tower crane absent from the Corran Valley site, October 2025 to April 2026
edges.to: Late completion of the structural frame

edges.from: Owner change orders CO-07 to CO-12
edges.to: Late completion of the structural frame

edges.from: Architect RFI responses exceeding the contractual response period
edges.to: Late completion of the structural frame
Decision to move the tower crane to the Kestrel project

actions.text: Submit the drafted 26-week extension-of-time and prolongation claim to Halden on 1 December as drafted.
Withdraw the drafted claim and settle the final account with Halden on the basis that the frame stoppage was Callerby's own responsibility.
Suspend the regional early-handover incentive scheme on the grounds that it drove the crane transfer.
Commission a second claims consultant to prepare an independent forensic delay analysis before deciding whether to submit any claim.
Issue the site superintendent a formal written warning for discussing the crane's whereabouts with Halden's clerk of works.
